textbookBox.concept: Yeru Thazhuvuthal (embracing the bull, widely known today as Jallikattu) is a non-lethal cultural sport rooted in Sangam life and Pongal harvest gratitude.

beats.en: Yeru Thazhuvuthal (embracing the bull, widely known today as Jallikattu) is a non-lethal cultural sport rooted in Sangam life and Pongal harvest gratitude.
beats.speakEn: Yeru Thazhuvuthal (embracing the bull, widely known today as Jallikattu) is a non-lethal cultural sport rooted in Sangam life and Pongal harvest gratitude.

beats.en: Yeru means a spirited bull, and Yeru Thazhuvuthal means embracing the rushing bull without weapons to tame it.

beats.en: Historically, Yeru Thazhuvuthal grew across Mullai (pastoral forest) and Marutham (fertile agricultural plains) landscapes.
beats.speakEn: Historically, Yeru Thazhuvuthal grew across Mullai (pastoral forest) and Marutham (fertile agricultural plains) landscapes.

beats.en: Today, it is celebrated across Tamil Nadu under names like Jallikattu (Sallikkattu), Manjuvirattu, and Veli Virattu during Pongal.
